facts.statement: The study was a prospective observational study of 68 children and adolescents with acquired brain injury, with an average age of 13.27 years.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants completed standardized tests to measure their ability to understand others' mental states and recognize emotions.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The severity of the brain injury was the strongest factor associated with performance on both mental state understanding and emotion recognition tests.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: General intelligence, measured by full-scale IQ, explained additional variation in mental state understanding performance beyond other injury and environmental factors.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: A longer time since the brain injury was associated with lower scores on mental state understanding tests.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The cause of the injury (traumatic versus non-traumatic) and the general location of the brain lesion (frontal versus non-frontal) did not significantly predict social cognition performance.
facts.subject: humans
